<antArtifact type="application/vnd.ant.code" language="javascript" identifier="route-page-functions" title="src/routes/page-routes.js">
const express = require("express");
const router = express.Router();
const { CONFIG } = require("../config/notion-config");
const { notionApi, apiCallWithRetry, handleApiError } = require("../utils/notion-api");
const { cache } = require("../utils/cache");
const { sanitizeInput, createParagraphBlock, createHeadingBlock, createPageTemplate } = require("../utils/block-helpers");
const { findPageByTitle, extractPageTitle, extractChildPages } = require("../utils/page-helpers");

// === List Pages (Enhanced) ===
router.get("/list-pages", async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const { limit = CONFIG.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, recursive = true } = req.query;
    const parsedLimit = parseInt(limit, 10);
    
    if (isNaN(parsedLimit) || parsedLimit < 1) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid limit parameter. Must be a positive number." });
    }
    
    console.log(`📄 Listing pages with limit=${parsedLimit}, recursive=${recursive}`);
    
    const results = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
      notionApi.post('/search', { page_size: parsedLimit })
    );

    const basePages = await Promise.all(
      results.data.results.map(async (item) => {
        try {
          const title = await extractPageTitle(item) || `Untitled (${item.id.substring(0, 8)})`;

          return {
            title,
            id: item.id,
            type: item.object,
            parent: item.parent?.page_id || item.parent?.database_id || null,
            url: item.url || null
          };
        } catch (err) {
          console.error(`Error processing page ${item.id}:`, err.message);
          return {
            title: `Error (${item.id.substring(0, 8)})`,
            id: item.id,
            type: item.object,
            parent: item.parent?.page_id || item.parent?.database_id || null,
            url: item.url || null,
            error: true
          };
        }
      })
    );

    const childPages = [];
    if (recursive === 'true' || recursive === true) {
      console.log(`🔍 Starting recursive page discovery for ${basePages.length} base pages`);
      const visited = new Set(); // Track visited pages to prevent duplicates
      
      // Process in batches of 5 to limit concurrent requests
      const batchSize = 5;
      for (let i = 0; i < basePages.length; i += batchSize) {
        const batch = basePages.slice(i, i + batchSize);
        await Promise.all(
          batch.map(base => {
            if (!visited.has(base.id)) {
              return extractChildPages(base.id, childPages, visited);
            }
            return Promise.resolve();
          })
        );
      }
      
      console.log(`✅ Completed recursive discovery, found ${childPages.length} child pages`);
    }

    // Use a Map to deduplicate pages by ID while keeping the most informative entry
    const pagesMap = new Map();

    // First add all base pages
    for (const page of basePages) {
      pagesMap.set(page.id, page);
    }

    // Then add child pages, but don't overwrite if the existing entry has a title
    // and the new one doesn't
    for (const page of childPages) {
      const existingPage = pagesMap.get(page.id);

      if (!existingPage || 
          (page.title && page.title !== "(no title)" && 
           (!existingPage.title || existingPage.title === "(no title)" || existingPage.title.includes("Untitled")))) {
        pagesMap.set(page.id, page);
      }
    }

    const uniquePages = Array.from(pagesMap.values());
    console.log(`📊 Returning ${uniquePages.length} unique pages`);
    
    res.json({ 
      success: true, 
      count: uniquePages.length, 
      pages: uniquePages 
    });
  } catch (error) {
    handleApiError(res, error, "list-pages");
  }
});

// === Write/Replace Content in Notion Page by Title with Versioning ===
router.put("/write-page-by-title", async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const { title, content, replace = false, maxVersionAttempts = 3 } = req.body;

    // Input validation
    if (!title || !content) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing title or content." });
    }

    if (typeof title !== 'string' || typeof content !== 'string') {
      return res.status(400).json({ 
        error: "Invalid input. Title and content must be strings." 
      });
    }
    
    const sanitizedTitle = sanitizeInput(title);
    const sanitizedContent = sanitizeInput(content);

    if (!sanitizedTitle) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Title cannot be empty after sanitization." });
    }

    // Create a helper function for version creation to support retry logic
    const createVersionedPage = async (baseTitle, content, attempt = 1) => {
      // Escape regex special characters in baseTitle for safe matching
      const safeTitle = baseTitle.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
      const titleRegex = new RegExp(`^${safeTitle}\\s+(\\d+)$`);

      // Search for all pages with similar titles
      const searchResults = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
        notionApi.post('/search', {
          query: baseTitle,
          filter: { property: "object", value: "page" },
          page_size: 100
        })
      );

      // Track versions and build version map for possible debugging
      let highestVersion = 0;
      const versionMap = new Map();

      // Process all search results to find existing versions
      for (const page of searchResults.data.results) {
        try {
          const extractedTitle = await extractPageTitle(page);
          if (extractedTitle) {
            const match = extractedTitle.match(titleRegex);
            if (match) {
              const version = parseInt(match[1], 10);
              if (!isNaN(version)) {
                versionMap.set(version, extractedTitle);
                if (version > highestVersion) {
                  highestVersion = version;
                }
              }
            }
          }
        } catch (err) {
          console.error(`Error processing version for page ${page.id}:`, err.message);
          // Continue with other pages
        }
      }

      // Calculate next version number
      const newVersion = highestVersion + 1;
      const versionSuffix = newVersion < 10 ? `0${newVersion}` : `${newVersion}`;
      const newTitle = `${baseTitle} ${versionSuffix}`;

      // Defensive check for existing page with the same versioned title
      const duplicateCheck = await findPageByTitle(newTitle);
      if (duplicateCheck) {
        console.warn(`Version collision detected for "${newTitle}"`);

        // Retry with exponential backoff if we haven't exceeded max attempts
        if (attempt < maxVersionAttempts) {
          console.log(`Retrying version creation (attempt ${attempt + 1}/${maxVersionAttempts})...`);
          // Wait with exponential backoff
          await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, Math.pow(2, attempt) * 500));
          return createVersionedPage(baseTitle, content, attempt + 1);
        }

        throw new Error(`Version collision persists after ${maxVersionAttempts} attempts`);
      }
      
      // Create the new versioned page
      console.log(`Creating new version: "${newTitle}" (version ${newVersion})...`);

      const childrenBlocks = [
        createHeadingBlock(newTitle),
        createParagraphBlock(`Version ${newVersion} of "${baseTitle}" - Created ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`),
        // Optional: Add metadata or version history information
        createHeadingBlock("Version History", 3)
      ];
      
      // Add version history paragraph
      const versionHistory = Array.from(versionMap.keys()).sort((a, b) => a - b);
      childrenBlocks.push(
        createParagraphBlock(`This is version ${newVersion}. Previous versions: ${versionHistory.join(', ') || 'None'}`)
      );
      
      // Add content section
      childrenBlocks.push(createHeadingBlock("Content", 2));
      
      // Handle content blocks (which might be an array after splitting long content)
      const contentBlocks = createParagraphBlock(content);
      if (Array.isArray(contentBlocks)) {
        childrenBlocks.push(...contentBlocks);
      } else {
        childrenBlocks.push(contentBlocks);
      }

      const createRes = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
        notionApi.post('/pages', {
          parent: { type: "page_id", page_id: CONFIG.NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID },
          properties: {
            title: [
              {
                type: "text",
                text: { content: newTitle }
              }
            ]
          },
          children: childrenBlocks
        })
      );

      return {
        pageId: createRes.data.id,
        newTitle,
        version: newVersion,
        versionHistory
      };
    };

    // Main execution logic
    console.log(`Attempting to write/replace page titled "${sanitizedTitle}"...`);
    const match = await findPageByTitle(sanitizedTitle);

    if (!match) {
      // Create first version of the page (no versioning needed yet)
      console.log(`Creating new page titled "${sanitizedTitle}"...`);
      
      const childrenBlocks = [
        createHeadingBlock(sanitizedTitle),
        createParagraphBlock(`Original version - Created ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`),
        createHeadingBlock("Content", 2)
      ];
      
      // Handle content blocks (which might be an array after splitting long content)
      const contentBlocks = createParagraphBlock(sanitizedContent);
      if (Array.isArray(contentBlocks)) {
        childrenBlocks.push(...contentBlocks);
      } else {
        childrenBlocks.push(contentBlocks);
      }
      
      const createRes = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
        notionApi.post('/pages', {
          parent: { type: "page_id", page_id: CONFIG.NOTION_PARENT_PAGE_ID },
          properties: {
            title: [
              {
                type: "text",
                text: { content: sanitizedTitle }
              }
            ]
          },
          children: childrenBlocks
        })
      );

      const pageId = createRes.data.id;

      // Invalidate cache after creating a new page
      cache.clear();

      return res.json({ 
        success: true, 
        created: true, 
        pageId,
        message: "Created new page (first version)"
      });
    } else {
      // Page exists, create a versioned page
      try {
        const result = await createVersionedPage(sanitizedTitle, sanitizedContent);

        // Invalidate cache after creating a new version
        cache.clear();

        return res.json({ 
          success: true, 
          created: true, 
          versioned: true, 
          originalTitle: sanitizedTitle,
          newTitle: result.newTitle,
          version: result.version,
          versionHistory: result.versionHistory,
          pageId: result.pageId,
          message: `Created new version ${result.version} of the page`
        });
      } catch (versionError) {
        // Handle version creation errors specifically
        console.error("Version creation failed:", versionError);
        return res.status(409).json({ 
          error: versionError.message || "Failed to create versioned page",
          suggestion: "Try again later or with a different title"
        });
      }
    }
  } catch (error) {
    handleApiError(res, error, "write-page-by-title");
  }
});

const express = require("express");
const router = express.Router();
const { CONFIG } = require("../config/notion-config");
const { notionApi, apiCallWithRetry, handleApiError } = require("../utils/notion-api");
const { sanitizeInput, normalizeKey } = require("../utils/block-helpers");

// === GET /notion/read-memory ===
router.get("/read-memory", async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const memoryDBId = CONFIG.NOTION_MEMORY_DB_ID;
    
    if (!memoryDBId) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing GPT_MEMORY in environment variables." });
    }
    
    const rawKey = req.query.key;
    let body = {};
    
    if (rawKey) {
      try {
        const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(rawKey);
        body = {
          filter: {
            property: "Key",
            title: { equals: normalizedKey }
          }
        };
      } catch (e) {
        return res.status(400).json({ 
          error: "Invalid key format.", 
          details: e.message 
        });
      }
    }

    const response = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
      notionApi.post(`/databases/${memoryDBId}/query`, body)
    );

    const memory = response.data.results.map(page => {
      const key = page.properties.Key?.title?.[0]?.plain_text || "(no key)";
      const value = page.properties.Value?.rich_text?.[0]?.plain_text || "";
      const lastUpdated = page.properties.LastUpdated?.date?.start || null;
      return { key, value, lastUpdated, id: page.id };
    });

    if (rawKey && memory.length === 0) {
      return res.status(404).json({ 
        error: `Memory key '${rawKey}' not found.`,
        message: "No matching memory entry found"
      });
    }

    res.json({ 
      success: true, 
      memory: rawKey ? memory[0] : memory,
      count: memory.length
    });
  } catch (err) {
    handleApiError(res, err, "read-memory");
  }
});

// === PATCH /notion/create-memory ===
router.patch("/create-memory", async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const memoryDBId = CONFIG.NOTION_MEMORY_DB_ID;
    const { line } = req.body;
    
    if (!memoryDBId) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing GPT_MEMORY in environment variables." });
    }
    
    if (!line || typeof line !== 'string' || !line.includes(":")) {
      return res.status(400).json({ 
        error: "Missing or malformed memory line. Format must be 'key: value'" 
      });
    }

    const [keyPart, ...rest] = line.split(":");
    
    // Validate key is not empty after normalization
    const key = normalizeKey(keyPart);
    if (!key) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Key cannot be empty." });
    }
    
    const value = rest.join(":").trim();
    if (!value) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Value cannot be empty." });
    }

    // Check if key already exists to avoid duplicates
    const existingQuery = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
      notionApi.post(`/databases/${memoryDBId}/query`, {
        filter: { property: "Key", title: { equals: key } }
      })
    );

    if (existingQuery.data.results.length > 0) {
      const existingId = existingQuery.data.results[0].id;
      
      // Update existing memory instead of creating a duplicate
      await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
        notionApi.patch(`/pages/${existingId}`, {
          properties: {
            Value: { rich_text: [{ text: { content: value } }] },
            LastUpdated: { date: { start: new Date().toISOString() } }
          }
        })
      );
      
      return res.json({ 
        success: true, 
        updated: true,
        pageId: existingId,
        message: `Updated existing memory with key '${keyPart.trim()}'`
      });
    }

    // Create new memory entry
    const response = await apiCallWithRetry(() => 
      notionApi.post('/pages', {
        parent: { database_id: memoryDBId },
        properties: {
          Key: { title: [{ text: { content: key } }] },
          Value: { rich_text: [{ text: { content: value } }] },
          LastUpdated: { date: { start: new Date().toISOString() } }
        }
      })
    );

    res.json({ 
      success: true, 
      created: true,
      pageId: response.data.id,
      message: `Created new memory with key '${keyPart.trim()}'`
    });
  } catch (err) {
    handleApiError(res, err, "create-memory");
  }
});

  try {
    const memoryDBId = CONFIG.NOTION_MEMORY_DB_ID;
    const { key, value } = req.body;

          LastUpdated: { date: { start: new Date().toISOString() } }
        }
      })
    );

    res.json({ 
      success: true, 
      message: `Memory updated for key '${key}'`,
      pageId
    });
  } catch (err) {
    handleApiError(res, err, "update-memory");
  }
});

    const memoryDBId = CONFIG.NOTION_MEMORY_DB_ID;

    if (!memoryDBId) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing GPT_MEMORY in environment variables." });

      });

I'll review the `notion.js` file thoroughly for any errors, syntax issues, performance concerns, or other problems. Let me analyze it section by section:

## Overall Structure Analysis

The file is a well-structured Express router for integrating with the Notion API. It includes:
- Environment variable validation
- API client setup with axios
- Caching mechanism
- Error handling
- Helper functions for working with Notion blocks
- Multiple route handlers for interacting with pages and databases
- Memory management functions

## Potential Issues

### 1. Error Handling & Reliability

The error handling pattern is generally good, but I see a few points for improvement:

- In `apiCallWithRetry`, the retry condition could be more comprehensive. For example, it doesn't handle network-level errors without response objects.

- The retry logic uses exponential backoff, which is good, but doesn't include any randomization (jitter) which could help prevent thundering herd problems if multiple clients experience failures simultaneously.

### 2. Cache Implementation

The cache implementation is functional but has some potential issues:

- The TTL is hardcoded to 5 minutes, which might not be optimal for all scenarios.
- The cleanup function only runs after an operation if it's been more than 10 minutes since the last cleanup, which could lead to memory bloat if the service has long periods of inactivity followed by intense usage.
- There's no maximum size limit for the cache, which could potentially cause memory issues if a large number of pages are cached.

### 3. Performance Concerns

- The `extractChildPages` function recursively fetches child pages, which could lead to a large number of API calls and potential rate limiting for deeply nested page structures.

- When appending content to pages, long content is split and appended in chunks of 10 blocks at a time, which is good for avoiding API limits. However, this could be made more efficient with batching and parallel processing where appropriate.

- The `paginatedRequest` helper function has a hardcoded maximum of 5000 items, which might be excessive for some use cases and could cause performance issues.

### 4. Code Redundancy

There's some redundancy in how page titles are extracted and managed. For example:
- Multiple places attempt to extract titles from different properties
- There are multiple code paths for creating/updating pages that share similar logic

### 5. Security Considerations

- Input validation is present but could be more robust in some areas. For example, there's limited sanitization of user input before using it in API calls or regex operations.

- The code doesn't appear to have any CSRF protection, which could be important if this API is exposed to browser clients.

### 6. Specific Code Issues

1. In the `createParagraphBlock` function, when splitting large content into chunks, the function might split content in the middle of words or HTML tags.

2. The `extractPageTitle` function has multiple fallback mechanisms, which is good, but it could potentially make multiple API calls for the same page if initial extraction attempts fail.

3. The error handling in some areas could lead to uncaught exceptions, for example in the recursive page extraction function.

4. The `normalizeKey` function uses `decodeURIComponent` which can throw errors with improperly formatted input.

## Recommendations

1. **Improved Error Handling**:
   - Add more comprehensive error handling in recursive functions
   - Include jitter in retry logic
   - Consider implementing circuit breaker patterns for API calls

2. **Cache Optimization**:
   - Add a maximum size limit for the cache
   - Make TTL configurable or adaptive based on usage patterns
   - Implement a more sophisticated cache eviction policy

3. **Performance Enhancements**:
   - Add batching for operations where possible
   - Implement pagination more consistently
   - Consider adding timeout parameters to API calls

4. **Code Quality**:
   - Refactor duplicate code into shared utility functions
   - Implement more comprehensive input validation
   - Consider using TypeScript for better type safety

Overall, the code is well-structured and includes many best practices like caching, retries, and proper error handling. The issues I've identified are mostly optimizations rather than critical flaws. The code should be functional as is, but could benefit from the improvements suggested above.

I'll analyze the `notion.js` file thoroughly to check for errors, code quality, efficiency, and opportunities for improvement. This is a comprehensive Notion API integration module with caching and memory management features.

## Overall Assessment

The code is generally well-structured and robust, with good error handling, retry mechanisms, and caching. However, there are a few issues and opportunities for improvement:

### Key Strengths

1. **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error handling with the `handleApiError` helper.
2. **Retry Logic**: Robust retry mechanism with exponential backoff and jitter.
3. **Caching**: Sophisticated caching system with TTL, cleanup, and multi-store support.
4. **Input Validation**: Good input sanitization and validation throughout routes.

### Issues and Improvement Opportunities

1. **Code Duplication**: There's one significant duplication in the initialization of `pagesMap`.
2. **Potential Memory Leak**: Cleanup interval is never cleared if the module is reloaded.
3. **Environment Variable Validation**: Good approach but can be enhanced.
4. **Some Long Functions**: A few functions are quite long and could be broken down further.
5. **Cache Usage Inconsistency**: Some routes don't use cache invalidation properly.

## Specific Issues

### 1. Code Duplication

There's a duplicated block of code around line 467-469:

```javascript
// First add all base pages
for (const page of basePages) {
  pagesMap.set(page.id, page);
}
// Use a Map to deduplicate pages by ID while keeping the most informative entry
const pagesMap = new Map();

// First add all base pages
for (const page of basePages) {
  pagesMap.set(page.id, page);
}
```

The `pagesMap` is declared and initialized twice. The first initialization is redundant and should be removed.

### 2. Potential Memory Leak

The cache cleanup interval is started but never cleared:

```javascript
startPeriodicCleanup() {
  setInterval(() => this.cleanup(), this.cleanupInterval);
}
```

For long-running applications where modules might be reloaded (dev environments, hot-reloading), this could lead to multiple interval timers running. Consider storing the interval ID and providing a way to clear it.

### 3. Error Handling in Block Processing

In some route handlers like `write-page-by-title`, there's a lot of complex logic for creating blocks that could benefit from additional error handling, especially when processing long content.

### 4. Cache Usage Inconsistency

Some routes invalidate specific cache entries, while others clear the entire cache. For better performance, consider more targeted cache invalidation.

### 5. Redundant API Calls

In some cases, like in the `extractTitleFromBlocks` function, there are nested API calls that could potentially be combined or parallelized.

## Code Efficiency Suggestions

1. **Batch Processing**: For operations that involve multiple API calls, consider using more Promise.all patterns to parallelize requests where appropriate.

2. **Consistent Cache Strategy**: Standardize when to invalidate vs. clear the entire cache.

3. **Function Decomposition**: Break down larger functions like `extractTitleUncached` and `createVersionedPage` into smaller, more focused functions.

4. **Memory Management**: Add explicit memory management for large data structures like search results.

5. **Request Timeouts**: The timeout mechanism is good, but consider adding more granular timeouts for different types of operations.

## Security Considerations

The code has good input sanitization but could benefit from:

1. **Rate Limiting**: Consider adding rate limiting for routes that allow write operations.

2. **Data Validation**: More thorough validation of incoming data, especially for routes that create or update content.

3. **Error Exposure**: Consider what error details are exposed in production vs. development environments.

## Conclusion

Overall, this is a well-implemented Notion integration with robust error handling, caching, and retry mechanisms. The main issues are minor and relate more to code organization and avoiding duplication rather than functional problems. The code effectively reuses helper functions where appropriate, but there are a few opportunities to further refactor and modularize some of the larger functions.

The module should work well for its intended purpose, and with the suggested improvements, it would be even more maintainable and efficient.
